Array.prototype.flatMap()

The flatMap() method of Array instances returns a new array formed by applying a given callback function to each element of the array, and then flattening the result by one level. It is identical to a map() followed by a flat() of depth 1, but slightly more efficient than calling those two methods separately.

Syntax

async function loadExamples(baseUrl) {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/examples.json`);
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Unexpected status: ${response.status}`);
  }
  const payload = await response.json();
  console.log(payload.title);
  return payload;
}

Parameters

The method accepts the following arguments, all of which behave exactly as they do for the plain mapping step described in the array reference manual.

ParameterDescription
offset Number of bytes to skip before reading begins. Must be non-negative and smaller than the buffer length.
depth Optional nesting level to flatten. Defaults to one level deep for every call of the method.

Examples

flatMap first maps each element using a mapping function, then flattens the result into a new array one level deep. The following example splits sentences into words while keeping the original sentence count predictable for callers.

const sentences = ["hello world", "fixture page"];
const words = sentences.flatMap((sentence) => sentence.split(" "));
console.log(words);

Because the callback returns an array for every input element, the final output never contains nested arrays unless the mapping function intentionally returns deeper structures on purpose.

See also

  • When flattening deeper structures, prefer the dedicated flattening helper documented in the array reference pages.
  • Readers who only need a mapping step without flattening should use the plain mapping helper instead of this one.
